messages:
chris-l: Heads-up — proposing a cutover for the policy negotiation layer this Friday. TL;DR: runtime will be able to "negotiate" a cost/latency boundary with the policy engine to pick a variant. Need alignment on API, signals, and rollout plan.

maya: Nice. Quick Q — is this a synchronous handshake per-request or async/heuristic? Concerned about extra RTT.

chris-l: Short answer: hybrid. Default is async cached negotiation (prefetch + periodic refresh) and a fast-sync fallback when cached decision is stale or tenant explicitly requests fresh. Goal is no extra RTT in common path.

sanjay: Agree hybrid. Can we define negotiation result TTL and how stale is stale? For bursty tenants TTL needs to be low.

alex-r: Proposed default TTL = 5s for hot prefixes, 60s otherwise. We should make this tenant-configurable.

maya: Works. Also need to clarify tie-breaker: when cost vs latency conflict which wins?

chris-l: Proposal: scoring function with tenant-configurable weights alpha/beta. Default: prefer latency for p95 < 200ms customers, else prefer cost. But we should also allow absolute thresholds (e.g., latency SLO hard limit).

alex-r: Example scoring: score = alpha * norm(latency_ms) + beta * norm(cost_usd_per_token). Normalization by historical 95th/median. Keep alpha/beta as small ints (default alpha=3, beta=1).

maya: Please add a hard SLO override: if predicted latency > latency_slo then immediate reject candidate (even if cheaper).

chris-l: Yup — implement as pre-filter before scoring.

 tom-infra: Implementation notes from runtime side: we'll need a compact proto between runtime <->policy with candidates list and quick score. Keep payload < 2KB. Also need route compatibility flags (kv-cache-friendly, supports-quantization) to filter.

chris-l: Draft API patch (WIP):
```http
POST /v1/policy/negotiate
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "tenant_id": "t-123",
  "prefix": "openai-ish prompt prefix...",
  "latency_slo_ms": 200,
  "budget_ms_per_token": 15,
  "candidates": [
    {"model": "redwood-7b-q4", "cost": 0.00012, "expected_latency_ms": 120, "flags": ["kv-cache"]},
    {"model": "redwood-13b-q8", "cost": 0.00035, "expected_latency_ms": 90, "flags": []}
  ],
  "mode": "default" // values: default, force_latency, force_cost
}
```

sanjay: For metrics we need: policy_negotiation.latency, policy_selection.cost_delta, policy_negotiation.failures, route_handshake_retries, negotiation_cache_hit_ratio. Also expose selected_candidate.* tags.

eva-prod: Also hook up quality gating: selection can't degrade eval-set scores beyond threshold. We'll run existing eval harness on canary traffic and compare.

maya: Rollout plan suggestion:
- Phase 0: internal-only (dev + staging) for 48h
- Phase 1: 10% canary on non-prod tenants in us-west for 24h
- Phase 2: 10% prod tenants (low qps) across two regions for 48h
- Phase 3: 50% ramp if metrics good
- Full flip after 1 week of stable metrics

sanjay: Canary pass conditions:
- p99 latency change <= +5% vs baseline
- p50/p95 within target
- cost reduction >= 5% for canary group
- no eval-set regressions > 1% absolute

chris-l: Ops-safety: add circuit-breaker that disables negotiation when negotiation_fail_rate > 1% for 10m or when negotiation adds >10ms median to request path. Circuit-breaker state to be surfaced in console and an alert.

 tom-infra: We'll add HTTP header `X-Policy-Negotiated: true|false` and `X-Policy-Decision: <model>` for observability. Runtime caches decision keyed by tenant+prefix-hash.

alex-r: Cache invalidation: when model metadata changes (e.g., quantization level or kernel swap) policy service will emit a `policy.cache.invalidate` event on pubsub with key patterns. Runtime subscribes and evicts. Also TTL fallback.

maya: Tests we need:
- unit tests for scoring math (alpha/beta boundary cases)
- integration: policy RPC + runtime selection under synthetic traces
- chaos: drop policy RPCs, ensure runtime fallback selects sensible default

eva-prod: Eval harness plan: run gen samples against baseline and negotiated routing and compute QA metrics. Use gating job that fails rollout if quality delta exceeds threshold.

chris-l: Backwards compat: older runtimes should treat negotiation as optional: if RPC errors or times out, runtime uses preconfigured static policy. We'll ship runtime to understand header and log negotiation_fallback reason.

sanjay: Security/privacy: negotiation request contains prompt prefix. Need to ensure we strip PII and only send hashed prefix + features. Add tenant-scrubbing middleware.

alex-r: We'll also expose tenant override via account settings in Console: weight sliders, hard SLOs, opt-out toggle. Product to design UI.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled cutover job created for Friday 20:00 UTC. Canary group definition: tag=policy-neg-canary.

maya: One more nit: define backoff strategy when negotiation is slow — exponential backoff with jitter and immediate fallback to static route on first failure.

chris-l: Agreed. I'll write the RFC follow-up doc with the decisions above and link PRs: policy-service change + runtime client lib + console flag + metrics dashboards + eval gating job. Ping me if you want to be added to reviewers.

alex-r: I'll own the SDK changes. tom-infra will own runtime. Sanjay will handle metrics/alerts. Maya/Eva handle eval and product.

chris-l: Thanks — I'll open a PR now and tag everyone. Quick reminder: keep negotiation payload minimal and no PII in transit. :thumbsup:

chris-l: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/policy-service/pull/402 (draft) — feedback welcome.

eva-prod: Looking. Will run eval harness once draft is stable.

chris-l: Final note: if anyone wants different default alpha/beta, speak now. Otherwise default alpha=3 beta=1 + hard SLO prefilter.

maya: fine from infra/product side.

sanjay: fine from metrics side.

alex-r: ok from SDK side.

tom-infra: okay. I'll queue runtime canary build.

chris-l: Cool — last_message. Putting cutover job in calendar and will follow the rollout playbook. Thanks all.
